blocks.text: Nobody wants to type 40-character hashes. A ref is a name that stores a commit hash. A branch is nothing more than a file containing the hash of its latest commit, which is why creating a branch in Git is instant.

$ cat .git/refs/heads/main
9c1e2f7a8b3d4c5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e

$ cat .git/HEAD
ref: refs/heads/main

# Refs may also be packed into one file for efficiency
$ cat .git/packed-refs
4b8d0a1... refs/remotes/origin/main
71a3e55... refs/tags/v1.0.0

rows: You commit, merge, reset or rebase on them
You fetch or pull (never by committing locally)

blocks.text: Always use git rev-parse, git show-ref or git for-each-ref in scripts instead of reading .git/refs files directly, because refs can live in packed-refs or, in newer setups, in the reftable format.

HEAD is a special ref that marks your current position. Normally it is a symbolic ref: it points to a branch, and the branch points to a commit. When you commit, Git creates the new commit with the current commit as parent, then moves the branch HEAD points to. HEAD follows along automatically.

blocks.src: generate: two panels; left panel 'attached HEAD': HEAD -> main -> commit C3, with C1 <- C2 <- C3 chain; right panel 'detached HEAD': HEAD pointing directly to commit C2 while main still points to C3
blocks.caption: Attached: HEAD points to a branch. Detached: HEAD points directly to a commit.

blocks.text: ~ moves up generations; ^ selects among parents. They only differ on merge commits. HEAD~2 is the grandparent via first parents; HEAD^2 is the second parent of a merge. On a non-merge commit, HEAD^2 does not exist.

If you check out something that is not a local branch, such as a commit hash, a tag or a remote-tracking branch, HEAD points directly at a commit. This is called detached HEAD. It is a normal, useful state, not an error.

$ git switch --detach v1.0.0     # or: git checkout v1.0.0
HEAD is now at 71a3e55 Add inventory model

$ git status
HEAD detached at v1.0.0

items: Inspecting or building an old release.
git bisect checks out commits in detached mode while it searches for a bug.
CI systems often check out an exact commit; actions/checkout on a pull request checks out a merge commit in detached HEAD state.
Trying a quick experiment you may throw away.

blocks.text: The Risk: Commits Nobody Points To

You can commit in detached HEAD, and HEAD moves forward with you. But no branch points at those commits. As soon as you switch elsewhere, they become unreachable and, after the reflog expires, garbage-collected.

$ git commit -m "Experiment"
[detached HEAD 5a7b9c1] Experiment

$ git switch main
Warning: you are leaving 1 commit behind, not connected to
any of your branches:
  5a7b9c1 Experiment

# Save it: create a branch at that commit
$ git branch experiment 5a7b9c1

# Or, while still detached, create a branch where you are
$ git switch -c experiment

$ git rev-parse HEAD               # resolve any revision to a full hash
$ git symbolic-ref HEAD            # which branch HEAD points to
refs/heads/main
$ git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname:short)' refs/heads
$ git update-ref refs/heads/hotfix 4b8d0a1   # move a ref safely
